extra.message: Unauthenticated GET /api/v2/user passes the name query parameter directly to eval(). An attacker can execute arbitrary JavaScript with the Node.js process's privileges, including filesystem access and operating-system commands.

cwe: CWE-95: Improper Neutralization of Directives in Dynamically Evaluated Code

extra.message: POST /api/v2/profile passes the attacker-controlled profile object directly as rendering options. An authenticated attacker can submit profile.layout='../../../package.json' to read files outside the views directory. The configured renderer joins layout to the views directory, reads it, and returns its rendered contents without requiring a template extension. This follows from the application's unrestricted options forwarding and the [hbs implementation](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/pillarjs/hbs/v4.1.1/lib/hbs.js).

cwe: CWE-22: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory

extra.message: PATCH /api/v1/tasks/:id authenticates the caller but selects and updates a task using only the supplied ID. Any registered user can modify another user's description or completion status. Task IDs are available through the unauthenticated legacy listing endpoint.

cwe: CWE-639: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key

extra.message: PATCH /api/v1/users/:id updates the supplied user ID without comparing it to req.user._id. Any authenticated user can change another account's name, email, password, or age. Because passwords are stored unchanged, supplying an attacker-generated bcrypt hash also permits subsequent login with the corresponding password.

cwe: CWE-639: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key

extra.message: DELETE /api/v1/users/:id calls findByIdAndDelete with the supplied ID without checking ownership or administrative permission. Any authenticated user can permanently delete another user's account.

cwe: CWE-639: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key

extra.message: GET /api/v1/tasks has no authentication middleware and returns Task.find({}). Anyone can retrieve every user's task descriptions, completion states, task IDs, and owner IDs.

cwe: CWE-306: Missing Authentication for Critical Function

extra.message: GET /api/v1/users/:name exposes user records without authentication. Anyone who supplies a matching name can obtain the account's email, age, and user ID. The toJSON method removes passwords and tokens but leaves these personal fields exposed.

cwe: CWE-306: Missing Authentication for Critical Function

extra.message: Unauthenticated GET /contact forwards the url query parameter directly to needle.get without restricting destinations. An attacker can cause requests to loopback, private-network, or metadata HTTP services accessible to the server. Response bodies are not returned, but internal requests and observable success/failure behavior remain available.

cwe: CWE-918: Server-Side Request Forgery

extra.message: GET /contact redirects to the attacker-supplied url after a successful outbound request. An attacker-controlled reachable website satisfies this condition, allowing a trusted application link to redirect visitors to a phishing destination.

cwe: CWE-601: URL Redirection to Untrusted Site

extra.message: Task descriptions returned by the API are interpolated into innerHTML without escaping. An attacker can store an HTML event-handler payload in another user's task through PATCH /api/v1/tasks/:id; it executes when that user opens the dashboard. Client-side stripHTML does not protect direct API submissions.

cwe: CWE-79: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation

extra.message: The decoded name URL parameter is concatenated into html at line 181 and assigned to resultsEl.innerHTML. Opening a crafted /contact.html?name= link containing an HTML event-handler payload executes attacker-controlled JavaScript in the application's origin.

cwe: CWE-79: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation

extra.message: The password field stores the submitted string without hashing. Registration saves new User(req.body), and both profile-update routes save password assignments directly; no password-hashing setter or save middleware exists. Database access therefore exposes users' submitted passwords. bcrypt.compare during login does not protect stored values.

cwe: CWE-256: Plaintext Storage of a Password

extra.message: Authentication tokens are signed with the hardcoded key 'hardsecret', also used by src/middleware/auth.js:8. Anyone with the source can generate valid signatures. Authentication additionally checks exact token membership in the database, so arbitrary forged tokens alone are rejected; however, predictable user IDs and issuance timestamps permit reconstruction of existing issued tokens.

cwe: CWE-321: Use of Hard-coded Cryptographic Key

extra.message: POST /dashboard passes req.body.email into this query without requiring a string. JSON input such as email={"$ne":null} or an attacker-controlled $regex becomes a database predicate instead of a literal email, changing account selection and permitting expensive regex queries. bcrypt comparison still occurs, so this is not an unconditional password bypass. Operator interpretation is consistent with [Mongoose query casting](https://mongoosejs.com/docs/5.x/docs/tutorials/query_casting.html).

cwe: CWE-943: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements in Data Query Logic

extra.message: Registration sets the authentication cookie without HttpOnly or Secure; login repeats this at line 36. Same-origin JavaScript can read the bearer token, enabling session theft through the confirmed XSS flows, and the browser can transmit it over HTTP.

cwe: CWE-1004: Sensitive Cookie Without 'HttpOnly' Flag
CWE-614: Sensitive Cookie in HTTPS Session Without 'Secure' Attribute

extra.message: JWTs are issued without exp or expiresIn and retained in user.tokens without an expiration timestamp. Authentication checks signature and membership but no session age. A stolen token remains usable indefinitely until explicitly removed, even after the browser's session cookie disappears.

cwe: CWE-613: Insufficient Session Expiration

extra.message: The dashboard logout button calls POST /api/v2/users/logout, which has no server route. The handler ignores the HTTP failure, deletes browser cookies, and displays the login page. The token remains in the database and can still authenticate subsequent requests, so previously copied tokens survive the apparent logout.

cwe: CWE-613: Insufficient Session Expiration

extra.message: GET /logout clears every authentication token using only cookie authentication, without CSRF validation. An attacker can cause a victim's browser to navigate to this URL and terminate all their sessions. Top-level cross-site GET navigation can carry cookies even with SameSite=Lax behavior.

cwe: CWE-352: Cross-Site Request Forgery

extra.message: The MongoDB service publishes port 27017 on all host interfaces without configuring authentication or credentials. A network client that can reach this port can directly read or modify application collections, including plaintext passwords and authentication tokens, bypassing Express authorization.

cwe: CWE-306: Missing Authentication for Critical Function

extra.message: Registration constructs User directly from req.body, allowing the caller to choose _id. Legacy account deletion uses findByIdAndDelete, which does not execute the document remove hook that deletes owned tasks. An attacker can register using a deleted account's exposed owner ID and receive a valid session owning its remaining tasks, including access through the otherwise ownership-checked v2 endpoints.

cwe: CWE-915: Improperly Controlled Modification of Dynamically-Determined Object Attributes
